summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) to route between lan-a (vtnet1↔node2, 10.50.1.0/24) and lan-b (vtnet2↔node3, 10.50.2.0/24), created a single named port-list alias NODE3_ALLOWED_TCP_PORTS (8080, 8443, 9000) in /conf/config.xml, and added one firewall pass rule on the lan-a interface referencing that alias for node2→node3 TCP traffic. Verified end-to-end TCP reachability on all three ports and confirmed an unlisted port (9001) stays blocked. Also completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes, proving changed boot identity and full recovery of routing, the alias/rule, and connectivity after each restart.
actions_performed: Discovered node1's OPNsense had only a management 'lan' interface configured; vtnet1/vtnet2 were unconfigured physical links to node2 and node3 respectively
Assigned static IPs via nmcli on node2 (10.50.1.10/24) and node3 (10.50.2.10/24) enp8s0 interfaces plus static routes to each other's subnet via node1
Added opt1 (lan-a, vtnet1, 10.50.1.254/24) and opt2 (lan-b, vtnet2, 10.50.2.254/24) interfaces to node1's config.xml and reconfigured them via configctl
Created a single OPNsense port alias 'NODE3_ALLOWED_TCP_PORTS' (8080, 8443, 9000) in config.xml under OPNsense/Firewall/Alias/aliases
Added one pass rule on interface opt1 (lan-a) for source 10.50.1.10 -> destination 10.50.2.10, protocol tcp, port referencing the alias, then ran configctl filter reload
Verified pf expanded the alias into 3 discrete port-match lines sharing one rule label, confirming single-rule/alias semantics
Diagnosed and fixed a secondary blocker: node3's own firewalld was rejecting inbound traffic on 8080/8443/9000 with admin-prohibited; opened those ports in firewalld's public zone
Verified end-to-end TCP connectivity for all 3 allowed ports from node2 to node3, and confirmed port 9001 (not in the alias) is blocked
Captured healthy baselines (boot markers, interface/route state, firewalld ports) on all three nodes before restarting
Restarted node1 (OPNsense) via 'shutdown -r now', polled until exec access returned, proved changed kern.boottime, and reverified persisted interfaces, pf rule/alias, and full connectivity
Restarted node2 via 'shutdown -r now', proved changed /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id, and reverified persisted static IP/route and connectivity
Restarted node3 via 'shutdown -r now', proved changed boot_id, and reverified persisted static IP/route, firewalld ports, and connectivity
Cleaned up temporary socat test listeners and tcpdump processes used for verification

evidence.requirement: Node1 routes between lan-a and lan-b (interfaces configured, forwarding enabled)
evidence.summary: node1 initially had only vtnet0(lan/mgmt) configured; vtnet1/vtnet2 had no IP. Added opt1/opt2 interfaces (lan-a/lan-b), reconfigured them, confirmed ip.forwarding=1, and pinged both node2 and node3 subnets successfully from node1.

evidence.requirement: Single named alias object containing ports 8080, 8443, 9000 on node1, referenced by the rule (not one rule per port)
evidence.summary: Added alias 'NODE3_ALLOWED_TCP_PORTS' with content 8080/8443/9000 and a single pass rule on opt1 referencing the alias by name in the destination port field; after 'configctl filter reload', pfctl -sr shows the alias correctly expanded to 3 port matches sharing one rule label (ef5120e9...), confirming one authored rule object drives all three ports.

evidence.requirement: node2 can reach node3 on TCP 8080, 8443, 9000; other ports remain blocked
evidence.summary: Baseline (pre-rule) connections to 8080/8443/9000 from node2 were CLOSED. After adding the alias-based OPNsense rule and opening the same ports in node3's firewalld (secondary host-level block discovered via pf logging), all three ports opened successfully and port 9001 (outside the alias) timed out (blocked).

evidence.requirement: Root-cause diagnosis of unexpected 'No route to host' errors
evidence.summary: pflog0 capture on node1 showed the SYN was correctly forwarded through OPNsense to node3, and node3 itself replied with an ICMP admin-prohibited filter message (its firewalld blocking the port), which is what fixed the remaining reachability issue.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured kern.boottime baseline (16:53:25); issued shutdown -r now (ack returned before disconnect); confirmed unreachable during reboot; polled until exec succeeded with new kern.boottime (17:00:32); verified opt1/opt2 IPs and alias-derived pf rule persisted; end-to-end TCP test on 8080/8443/9000 succeeded post-restart.

evidence.requirement: Node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id baseline (b953e8ce...); issued shutdown -r now; confirmed connection timed out during reboot; polled until boot_id changed to a3a25632...; verified static IP/route to node3 subnet persisted; TCP connectivity to node3's 8080/8443/9000 succeeded post-restart.

evidence.requirement: Node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id baseline (03273aa8...) plus firewalld port state; issued shutdown -r now; confirmed connection timed out during reboot; polled until boot_id changed to 991eed2c...; verified static IP/route and firewalld port openings (8080/8443/9000) persisted; end-to-end connectivity from node2 confirmed post-restart.
